pride_data.title: Proximity labeling – LC/MS-MS with ERC1-TurboID/atg7-2 Arabidopsis seedlings
pride_data.projectDescription: Given that ERC1 proteins are enriched on membraneless condensates together with ATG8 proteins prior to autophagosome formation, we hypothesized that ERC1-positive condensates might serve as an assembly site for ATG8 proteins and other adaptors before ATG8 proteins are conjugated onto the phagophore membrane. In order to identify other possible components related to the ERC1 condensates, we generated transgenic plants expressing TurboID-tagged ERC1 in the atg7-2 background. TurboID-coupled mass spectrometry revealed that, in addition to ATG8e, the selective autophagy receptor NBR1 was also significantly enriched.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Arabidopsis seedlings expressing ERC1-TurboID under the UBQ10 promoter in atg7-2 or TurboID under the UBQ10 promoter were grown on ½ MS plates containing 1% sucrose for 5 days. Seedlings were harvested and submerged in ½ MS + 1% sucrose supplemented with 50 µM biotin for 1 h followed by washing and flash freezing. Proteins were extracted by resuspending the ground plant material in extraction buffer (50 mM TrisHCl pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 0.1% SDS, 1% Triton-X-100, 0.5% Na-deoxycholate, 1 mM EGTA, 1 mM DTT, 1× complete Protease inhibition cocktail, 1 mM PMSF), incubating for 15 minutes at 4°C on a rotor wheel, sonicating four times for 30 seconds and centrifuging at 15,000 g at 4°C for 15 minutes. The clear supernatant was subjected to a 7k Zeba Spin desalting column (Thermo Fisher) to remove excess biotin using extraction buffer (50 mM TrisHCl pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 0.1% SDS, 1% Triton-X-100, 0.5% Na-deoxycholate, 1 mM EGTA, 1 mM DTT, 1× complete Protease inhibition cocktail, 1 mM PMSF). Eluted proteins were incubated with Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin T1 (Invitrogen, 150 μl) overnight at 4°C for affinity purification of biotinylated proteins. The beads were then washed with the following buffers: 2x with cold extraction buffer, 2x with equilibration buffer (50 mM TrisHCl pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 0.1% SDS, 1% Triton-X-100, 0.5% Na-deoxycholate, 1 mM EGTA, 1 mM DTT), 1x with cold 1M KCl, 1x with cold 100 mM Na2CO3, 1x with Urea wash buffer 1 (2 M Urea, 50 mM Tris pH 7.5, room temperature) and 2x with 50 mM Tris pH 7.5.  For on-beads tryptic digest, the streptavidin beads were further washed 2x with Urea wash buffer 2 (50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 1 M Urea), followed by three hours incubation in Trypsin buffer (50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 1 M Urea, 1 mM DTT, 0.4 µg Trypsin) at 25°C. The supernatant from tryptic digest and two washes with 60 µl 1 M Urea in 50 mM Tris pH 7.5 were reduced and alkylated and digested overnight with 0.5 µg Trypsin. The digest was acidified by adding formic acid to a final concentration of ~ 1 % and desalted using C18 spin column.  LC-MS/MS was done on a Orbitrap Fusion Lumos Tribrid Mass Spectrometer (Thermo Fisher), equipped with an LC UltiMate 3000 RSLCnano system (Thermo Fisher). Peptides were separated using analytical column C18 (Thermo Fisher). The flow rate was 300 nl/min and a 120-min gradient was used. Peptides were eluted using mobile phase A [1.9% acetonitrile (ACN), 0.1% FA] and mobile phase B (98% ACN, 0.1% FA). The following LC gradient was used as follows: 100% A for the initial 5 min, then 0% to 6% B for 3 min, then 6% B to 30% B for 42 min, then 30% B to 45% B for 10 min, then 45% B to 60% B for 10 min, then 60% B to 80% B for 5 min and an additional 5 min at 80% B followed by final re-equilibrium with 100% A for 10 min.  The precursor scan range was m/z 375–1,500. Higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) was performed with a normalized collision energy of 30. The isolation window was set to m/z 1.6, with a maximum injection time of 22 ms and an Orbitrap resolution of 15,000.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: Peptide identification and quantification of the mass spectrometry data was carried out using MaxQuant Version 2.4.12.0.  The data was searched against the Arabidopsis TAIR 10 protein database obtained from TAIR (TAIR10_pep_20101214.fasta) containing a total of 35386 entries and against the contaminants list of MaxQuant. All three control and experimental samples were analyzed simultaneously using the default settings with matching between runs turned on. Label free quantification (LFQ) was enabled with the minimum ratio count set to two. To analyze the resulting proteomic data, the identified protein groups and their LFQ intensities from the MaxQuant search were loaded into Perseus Version 2.1.3.0. Data were filtered to remove decoys, potential contaminants, and protein groups that were only identified by site (i.e., posttranslational modification). LFQ intensities were log2 transformed, and only protein groups that had valid values for either all three experimental samples or all three control samples were kept, an operation that eliminated non-reproducible identifications. Remaining invalid values were replaced with imputed values from a normal distribution downshifted by 1.8 with a width of 0.3 made from all matrix values. A two-sided T-test with S0 = 2 and FDR = 0.01 was used to determine the significance and enrichment of each protein group.
